If your favorite Twitter user has been shadow banned and you're wondering how to follow all their tweets, RSS feeds can help.

If you're worried about your clicks being redirected to false sites, RSS feeds can help.

If you're worried about surfing the web anonymously, RSS feeds can help.

Obviously using RSS feeds won't completely address all your concerns, but using RSS feeds is a big help.

RSS feeds track when new content is posted to a website. If voat.co/v/qrv had an RSS feed, every new post would be a new hit in your feed. The interface is a lot like email. Getting a new hit is like getting a new message. You can organize them into folders or whatever you want.

You can convert Twitter user's posts to a feed using either of the following sites:

https://twitrss.me

https://queryfeed.net

So for instance, you can have POTUS tweets sent to your RSS reader. You can also do feed based on a Twitter search. For example, if you want to know if people are protesting, you can do a search for the word protest.

But suppose you want to know if people are protesting in your city. You can do a geocode search along with the word protest. Easiest way to do this is with Queryfeed. It's self explanatory.

However, if for some reason you want to do it using twitrss.me, you'd use the second box on the page and type in the following:

geocode:lat,long,radius protest

"lat" = latitude coordinates for the center of your city (or maybe your house) in decimal format (no need to be too precise).

"long" = longitude, decimal format

"radius" = the geographic search area from the center, which has to be expressed in km or mi. So maybe you'd do 25mi for 25 miles.

Note: no spaces after the colon or the commas. Like this: protest geocode:45.5426225,-122.7944718,25mi

Then it'll direct you here: https://twitrss.me/twitter_search_to_rss/?term=protest+geocode%3A45.5426225%2C-122.7944718%2C25mi

That's the link to the RSS feed that you can add to your RSS reader. See the = right before the word protest in the link? Everything up to that point will always be the same for any search feed.

For user feeds, it looks like this: https://twitrss.me/twitter_user_to_rss/?user=realDonaldTrump

Again, everything before the = looks the same every time. (Note: for some reason POTUS twitter feed isn't working just now. I have it in my feeds, so don't know what's up with that. Use Queryfeed instead.)

Anyway, you can copy either link up to and including the = and then just add whatever you want and put it in your RSS reader.

Feedly is a great online tool that you can use to gather your favorite sites into one place. They also have iOS and Adroid apps. However, you should know that Feedly is owned by the evil and dastardly Google. Might want to think about which email address you use to sign up. Also, even if you use a gmail account as your email address to sign up, don't login using Google, but just login using Feedly, as if you had some other email address. That way, you can bypass LOGGING IN to Google with their stupid all controlling web-based pop up thing that logs you into every Google service imaginable.

Some people use RSS readers in Firefox, but it might be better not to have it in your browser. Instead, you can add it to Outlook (if you use it) or even in Thunderbird, which also has an RSS reader. You don't have to add an email address and all the stuff will be saved on your computer, not anywhere online.

RSS feeds are very helpful, but obviously not the solution to every problem. Nonetheless, give it a try.
